blocks.text: Dear Ms. Kipphorn:
section_path: DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH AND HUMAN SERVICES
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Please refer to your Supplemental Biologics License Application (sBLA), dated and received December 15, 2016, and your amendments, submitted under section 351(a) of the Public Health Service Act for Stelara ® (ustekinumab).
section_path: DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH AND HUMAN SERVICES
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: This Prior Approval supplemental biologics application provides for extension of the psoriasis indication to include treatment of adolescent patients ages 12-17 years.
section_path: DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH AND HUMAN SERVICES
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: APPROVAL & LABELING
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: We have completed our review of this supplemental application, as amended. It is approved, effective on the date of this letter, for use as recommended in the enclosed, agreed-upon labeling text.
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: CONTENT OF LABELING
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: As soon as possible, but no later than 14 days from the date of this letter, submit, via the FDA automated drug registration and listing system (eLIST), the content of labeling [21 CFR 601.14(b)] in structured product labeling (SPL) format, as described at http://www.fda.gov/ForIndustry/DataStandards/StructuredProductLabeling/default.htm, that is identical to the enclosed labeling (text for the prescribing information, text for the instructions for use, Medication Guide) and include the labeling changes proposed in any pending "Changes Being Effected" (CBE) supplements. Information on submitting SPL files using eLIST may be found in the guidance for industry titled "SPL Standard for Content of Labeling Technical Qs and As" at
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: http://www.fda.gov/downloads/Drugs/GuidanceComplianceRegulatoryInformation/Guidances/U CM072392.pdf.
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: The SPL will be accessible via publicly available labeling repositories.
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Food and Drug Administration Silver Spring MD 20993
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: SUPPLEMENT APPROVAL
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: page_footer
blocks.text: Reference ID: 4167129
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: page_header
blocks.text: BLA 125261/S-138 Page 2
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Also within 14 days, amend all pending supplemental applications that include labeling changes for this BLA, including pending "Changes Being Effected" (CBE) supplements, for which FDA has not yet issued an action letter, with the content of labeling [21 CFR 601.12(f)] in MS Word format that includes the changes approved in this supplemental application.
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: REQUIRED PEDIATRIC ASSESSMENTS
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Under the Pediatric Research Equity Act (PREA) (21 U.S.C. 355c), all applications for new active ingredients, new indications, new dosage forms, new dosing regimens, or new routes of administration are required to contain an assessment of the safety and effectiveness of the product for the claimed indication(s) in pediatric patients unless this requirement is waived, deferred, or inapplicable.
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: We are waiving the pediatric study requirement for ages under 6 years, because necessary studies are impossible or highly impracticable. This is because the number of pediatric patients under the age of 6 years with psoriasis is so small.
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: We note that you have partially fulfilled the pediatric study requirement for ages 12 to 17 years for this application.
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: We are deferring submission of your pediatric study for ages 6 to 12 years for this application until additional safety and effectiveness data have been collected.
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Your deferred pediatric study required by section 505B(a) of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act are required postmarketing study. The status of this postmarketing study must be reported annually according to 21 CFR 601.28 and section 505B(a)(3)(B) of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act. This required study is listed below.
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: 2331-1: Complete the ongoing open-label study CNTO1275PSO3013, assessing the efficacy, safety, and pharmacokinetics of subcutaneously administered ustekinumab in pediatric subjects ≥6 to <12 years of age with moderate to severe chronic plaque psoriasis.
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Study Completion: 02/2019
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Final Report Submission: 08/2019
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Submit the protocol(s) to your IND 09590, with a cross-reference letter to this BLA.
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Reports of this required pediatric postmarketing study must be submitted as a BLA or as a supplement to your approved BLA with the proposed labeling changes you believe are warranted based on the data derived from these studies. When submitting the reports, please clearly mark your submission "SUBMISSION OF REQUIRED PEDIATRIC ASSESSMENTS" in large font, bolded type at the beginning of the cover letter of the submission.
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: You may request advisory comments on proposed introductory advertising and promotional labeling. To do so, submit, in triplicate, a cover letter requesting advisory comments, the proposed materials in draft or mock-up form with annotated references, and the prescribing information to:
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: OPDP Regulatory Project Manager Food and Drug Administration Center for Drug Evaluation and Research Office of Prescription Drug Promotion 5901-B Ammendale Road Beltsville, MD 20705-1266
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Alternatively, you may submit a request for advisory comments electronically in eCTD format. For more information about submitting promotional materials in eCTD format, see the draft Guidance for Industry (available at:
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: http://www.fda.gov/downloads/Drugs/GuidanceComplianceRegulatoryInformation/Guidances/U CM443702.pdf ).
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: As required under 21 CFR 601.12(f)(4), you must submit final promotional materials, and the prescribing information, at the time of initial dissemination or publication, accompanied by a Form FDA 2253. Form FDA 2253 is available at http://www.fda.gov/downloads/AboutFDA/ReportsManualsForms/Forms/UCM083570.pdf. Information and Instructions for completing the form can be found at http://www.fda.gov/downloads/AboutFDA/ReportsManualsForms/Forms/UCM375154.pdf. For
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: more information about submission of promotional materials to the Office of Prescription Drug
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Promotion (OPDP), see http://www.fda.gov/AboutFDA/CentersOffices/CDER/ucm090142.htm.
blocks.speaker: regulator
